Model 4: Skew-Normal Niche (Azzalini & Capitanio 1999)

Source: vignettes/model_skew_normal.Rmd
model_skew_normal.Rmd

1 Ecological Motivation

Many species exhibit asymmetric environmental tolerances: they may tolerate higher temperatures much better than lower temperatures (or vice versa), so the niche boundary is not symmetric around the optimum. The multivariate normal model (Models 1–3) forces ellipsoidal symmetry, which can misfit such species.

The skew-normal model extends the Gaussian niche with a skewness parameter vector α∈ℝp\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^p that allows each environmental axis to have an asymmetric tail. The density is the multivariate skew-normal distribution of Azzalini and Capitanio (1999).

2 Mathematical Specification

2.1 Density

The pp-dimensional skew-normal density is

fSN(𝐱;μ,Σ,α)=2ϕp(𝐱−μ;Σ)Φ(∑k=1pαk(xk−μk)σk), f_{\text{SN}}(\mathbf{x};\mu,\Sigma,\alpha) = 2\,\phi_p(\mathbf{x}-\mu;\Sigma)\, \Phi\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^{p}\frac{\alpha_k(x_k - \mu_k)}{\sigma_k}\right), \tag{1}

where:

  • ϕp(⋅;Σ)\phi_p(\cdot;\Sigma) is the pp-variate normal density with covariance Σ\Sigma,
  • Φ(⋅)\Phi(\cdot) is the standard univariate normal CDF,
  • α=(α1,…,αp)⊤\alpha = (\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_p)^\top is the skewness vector,
  • σk=Σkk\sigma_k = \sqrt{\Sigma_{kk}} are the marginal standard deviations.

When α=𝟎\alpha = \mathbf{0}, Φ(0)=1/2\Phi(0) = 1/2 and the density reduces to ϕp\phi_p, recovering the symmetric Gaussian niche.

2.2 The Skewness Mechanism

Define the standardised skew score

zi=∑k=1pαk(xik−μk)σk=𝛂⊤diag⁡(σ)−1(𝐱i−μ). z_i = \sum_{k=1}^{p}\frac{\alpha_k(x_{ik} - \mu_k)}{\sigma_k} = \boldsymbol\alpha^\top\,\operatorname{diag}(\sigma)^{-1}(\mathbf{x}_i - \mu). \tag{2}

The factor Φ(zi)\Phi(z_i) modulates the Gaussian density:

  • When zi≫0z_i \gg 0 (the point is in the direction favoured by α\alpha), Φ(zi)≈1\Phi(z_i) \approx 1 and the density is close to 2ϕp2\phi_p.
  • When zi≪0z_i \ll 0 (the point is in the opposite direction), Φ(zi)≈0\Phi(z_i) \approx 0 and the density is suppressed.

This creates an asymmetric niche that is elongated in the direction of α\alpha and truncated in the opposite direction.

2.3 Negative Log-Likelihood

Given nn presence records:

−ℓ(θ)=n2log⁡|Σ|+12∑i=1nqi−∑i=1nlog⁡Φ(zi)+penalty, -\ell(\theta) = \frac{n}{2}\log|\Sigma| + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{n} q_i - \sum_{i=1}^{n}\log\Phi(z_i) + \text{penalty}, \tag{3}

where:

  • qi=∥L−1(𝐱i−μ)∥2q_i = \|L^{-1}(\mathbf{x}_i - \mu)\|^2 (squared Mahalanobis distance),
  • ziz_i is defined in Eq. (2),
  • The constants nlog⁡2n\log 2 and −np2log⁡(2π)-\frac{np}{2}\log(2\pi) are dropped (they do not affect the optimum and match the convention in Models 1–3).

2.4 Prior Penalties

The skew-normal model uses ridge penalties on both log⁡σ\log\sigma and α\alpha:

penalty=λσ∑k=1p(log⁡σk−ck)2+λα∑k=1pαk2, \text{penalty} = \lambda_\sigma\sum_{k=1}^{p}(\log\sigma_k - c_k)^2 + \lambda_\alpha\sum_{k=1}^{p}\alpha_k^2, \tag{4}

where ck=log⁡σ̂k(env_occ)c_k = \log\hat\sigma_k(\text{env\_occ}). The α\alpha penalty prevents extreme skewness that would effectively make one tail of the niche a step function.

3 Parameterisation

The unconstrained parameter vector θ\theta has length 3p+p(p−1)/23p + p(p-1)/2:

θ=[μ⏟p,log⁡σ⏟p,vC-vine⏟p(p−1)/2,α⏟p]. \theta = \bigl[\underbrace{\mu}_{p},\; \underbrace{\log\sigma}_{p},\; \underbrace{v_{\text{C-vine}}}_{p(p-1)/2},\; \underbrace{\alpha}_{p}\bigr].

Block Length Constraint Meaning
μ\mu pp Unconstrained Niche centroid
log⁡σ\log\sigma pp σk>0\sigma_k > 0 via exp\exp Marginal standard deviations
vv p(p−1)/2p(p-1)/2 Unconstrained C-vine partial correlations
α\alpha pp Unconstrained Skewness parameters

Note the α\alpha block is appended after the C-vine block, at position θ[2p+nv…3p+nv−1]\theta[2p + n_v \dots 3p + n_v - 1].

4 Implementation Call Chain 

optimize_niche(likelihood = "skew_normal")
  └─ niche_obj.cpp::create_niche_obj_ptr()
       └─ loglik_niche_math_skew_normal_eigen()    [C++, lines 543–583]
            ├─ build_L_cov()                        [theta → mu, sigma, L_cov]
            ├─ alpha = Map(theta + 2*p + n_v, p)    [line 559]
            ├─ Mahalanobis q via forward solve       [lines 565–566]
            ├─ log_det = 2 * sum log L_cov(k,k)     [lines 568–570]
            ├─ sum_log_phi = sum_log_pnorm(diff, sigma, alpha)  [line 572]
            ├─ prior_penalty_value(has_alpha=true)   [lines 578–579]
            └─ neg_log = 0.5*n*log_det + 0.5*sum_q - sum_log_phi + penalty

4.1 Key Code (loglik_niche_math_cpp.cpp, lines 543–583)

The C++ kernel:

  1. Reconstructs LcovL_{\text{cov}} from θ\theta via build_L_cov() (line 557).
  2. Maps the α\alpha block from θ\theta (line 559).
  3. Computes Mahalanobis distances via forward solve (lines 565–566).
  4. Computes log⁡|Σ|\log|\Sigma| from the Cholesky diagonal (lines 568–570).
  5. Evaluates ∑ilog⁡Φ(zi)\sum_i \log\Phi(z_i) via sum_log_pnorm() (line 572), which internally calls skew_z() (lines 520–527) to compute zi=α⊤diag⁡(σ)−1diffiz_i = \alpha^\top\operatorname{diag}(\sigma)^{-1}\text{diff}_i and then R::pnorm(..., log_p=1) (line 515) for numerically stable log⁡Φ\log\Phi.
  6. Adds the ridge penalty via prior_penalty_value() (lines 578–579).
  7. Returns the guarded negative log-likelihood (line 581).

4.2 Helper Functions

Function Lines Purpose
log_pnorm(z) 514–516 Stable log⁡Φ(z)\log\Phi(z) via R::pnorm
skew_z(diff, sigma, alpha) 520–527 Vectorised zi=(α/σ)⊤diffiz_i = (\alpha/\sigma)^\top\text{diff}_i
sum_log_pnorm(diff, sigma, alpha) 530–537 ∑ilog⁡Φ(zi)\sum_i\log\Phi(z_i)

4.3 R Entry Point 

optimize_niche(env_occ, likelihood = "skew_normal",
               prior_log_sigma_lambda = 1.0,
               prior_alpha_lambda = 1.0)

5 When To Use

  • When ecological knowledge or exploratory analysis suggests asymmetric environmental tolerances (e.g. thermal tolerance asymmetry in ectotherms).
  • As a model-selection candidate: fit both "presence_only" (symmetric) and "skew_normal" (asymmetric), then compare via AIC/BIC.
  • When the sample size is large enough to estimate pp additional parameters reliably (n≫3p+p(p−1)/2n \gg 3p + p(p-1)/2).

6 Limitations

  1. Additional parameters. The skewness vector adds pp parameters. For p=5p = 5 environmental variables, the total parameter count goes from 2p+p(p−1)/2=202p + p(p-1)/2 = 20 to 3p+p(p−1)/2=253p + p(p-1)/2 = 25. With small nn, the extra parameters may not be well-identified.

  2. Unimodal skewness. The skew-normal is still unimodal; it cannot capture bimodal niches.

  3. No background correction. This is a presence-only model. For background-corrected skew-normal, use "skew_normal_weighted" (Model 5).

  4. Near-singular Φ\Phi. When |zi||z_i| is very large, log⁡Φ(zi)\log\Phi(z_i) can be numerically challenging. The implementation uses R::pnorm with log_p = TRUE, which is stable for zz down to about −37-37.

References

Azzalini, A., and A. Capitanio. 1999. “Statistical Applications of the Multivariate Skew Normal Distribution.” Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B 61 (3): 579–602. https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9868.00194.
